title: Siloed probe scheduler and goldens sync for customer-scoped evals (privacy-first)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a privacy-first orchestration layer for running customer-scoped eval probes on Dedicated/Private deployments. The feature comprises a local probe scheduler (runs only inside a customer's VPC/on-prem instance), an encrypted goldens sync mechanism (one-way, customer-managed keys), and a lightweight telemetry gate that emits only aggregated, opt-in metrics. Goal: detect regressions triggered by config/model changes without exfiltrating sensitive customer data or goldens content.
acceptance_criteria: Probe scheduler can be deployed as a sidecar or system service inside Private/Dedicated control plane and be enabled per-customer via a flag.
Goldens are stored encrypted with customer KMS/HSM and can be synced from Redwood control plane in a one-way push that cannot retrieve plaintext from Redwood.

Telemetry emitted by the scheduler is opt-in and provides only aggregated pass/fail counts and latency histograms; raw model outputs are never sent to Redwood unless explicitly allowed by customer config.

Config/model change events (api: model pin update, runtime quantization toggle, routing policy change) trigger scheduled probes and produce an actionable regression report in the Console with diffed metrics and example redacted prompts.

Canary and rollback hooks: when a regression crosses threshold, the system creates an alert, attaches relevant probe run artifacts (redacted), and triggers a configurable rollback/circumvention policy.
End-to-end tests and a staging demo workspace showing a Private deployment running local probes against a model-variant change.
tasks: Design API for probe scheduling and per-customer opt-in flags (PM + Eng + Security)
Define goldens packaging format and one-way sync protocol using customer KMS
Implement sidecar scheduler prototype for Private deployment (ENG)
Telemetry gate: implement aggregator and opt-in consent UI in Console (DX/Product)
Integrate trigger hooks for config/model change events in orchestration layer
Create Console regression report UI and alerting templates
Write e2e tests, privacy audit checklist, and run privacy threat model review
notes: 2025-02-18: Triage completed. Priority set to P1 due to several Dedicated customers requesting isolated regression detection for config rollouts.
2025-02-24: Design workshop with Security and Infra — decided on three pillars: local-only scheduling, one-way goldens push, opt-in aggregated telemetry. Confluence RFC drafted.
2025-02-27: Trade-off discussion: allowing server-side evals is faster for productization but unacceptable for some customers; default to local-scheduler with controlled exceptions.
2025-03-01: Engineering spike finished. Prototype sidecar runs scheduled jobs and writes results to a local S3-compatible store. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/probes/pull/198
2025-03-03: Security review notes: require customer-managed KMS for goldens and HSM recommended for on-prem; telemetry must be sampled and hashed before export. Added to task list.
2025-03-05: PM review with Solutions Eng. Action: prepare partner-facing runbook and customer consent UI copy. Assigned UI copy to Design.
risks: Goldens sync complexity across air-gapped installs (will require separate signed bundle process)
Potential latency of local probes delaying alerting; need to tune schedule vs. change window
Misconfiguration by customer could lead to accidental plaintext export — mitigated by defaulting to local-only and strong UI warnings
owner_notes: Aim for a minimal MVP that supports policy-driven probe schedules and demonstrates model-change detection for three customers in Dedicated staging.
Coordinate with Console team for the consent flow; keep telemetry conservative by default.
Plan a follow-up (PM-24020) to add evaluation result explainability and automatic golden-updates workflow if customers opt in.
